text:
ConocoPhillips gained roughly 0.08% today to close at $137.46, continuing a strong two-week rally of 5.45% driven by escalating geopolitical tensions that are tightening global oil supplies. A critical Saudi Arabian pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz was shut down after attacks from Iran-allied groups, and Ukraine-Russia conflict continues disrupting Russian energy infrastructure—both events push crude prices higher (US oil at $97.26/barrel, world oil at $109.51/barrel), which directly benefits oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

These supply fears are compounding: traders are now betting gas prices will hit yearly highs, and U.S. diesel has already reached record levels above $6 per gallon. For an oil producer, a tighter supply environment and higher prices translate to stronger margins and higher revenues, which explains why the stock has steadily climbed over the past two weeks even as today's specific move was modest.
